entry.title: Entry #296 in Crowder v. LinkedIn Corporation, 4:22-cv-00237
entry.summary: DISCOVERY ORDER addressing 288 Discovery Letter Brief.The attached order addresses the parties' discovery letter brief. It orders as follows:Within two court days of this order, the plaintiffs must identify up to twenty-five privilege -log entries for in camera review. The plaintiffs choose the entries, but the selection should span the challenged categories. LinkedIn then must lodge them for in camera review and include the selected documents in unredacted form (with the produced redacted versions for comparison where applicable and the corresponding privilege log entries). LinkedIn also must provide updated privilege logs.This resolves ECF No. 288.Signed by Judge Laurel Beeler on 9/10/2026.(lblc2, COURT STAFF) (Filed on 9/10/2026)

entry.title: Entry #293 in Crowder v. LinkedIn Corporation, 4:22-cv-00237
Entry #292 in Crowder v. LinkedIn Corporation, 4:22-cv-00237
entry.summary: DISCOVERY ORDER addressing 285 Discovery Letter Brief.The attached order addresses the parties' discovery letter brief. It orders as follows:1. The plaintiffs' motion to compel LinkedIn to run the generative-AI search string acro ss four custodians and produce responsive documents hitting on the search string is granted. The plaintiffs' separate request to reopen depositions based on any newly-produced documents hitting on the search string is denied without prejudice.2. The plaintiffs' motion to compel unredacted or less-redacted versions of the two documents clawed back by LinkedIn is denied without prejudice. The plaintiffs may renew their motion by submitting the documents to the court for in camera r eview, which LinkedIn does not oppose.3. The plaintiffs' motion to reopen Mr. Pradhan's deposition is granted. The plaintiffs may examine Mr. Pradhan for one hour, remotely, with examination limited to any non-privileged discussions he had with counsel regarding his testimony during breaks at his August 24, 2026, deposition.This resolves ECF No. 285.Signed by Judge Laurel Beeler on September 10, 2026.(lblc2, COURT STAFF) (Filed on 9/10/2026)

Entry #274 in Crowder v. LinkedIn Corporation, 4:22-cv-00237
entry.summary: DISCOVERY ORDER addressing 268 Discovery Letter Brief.The attached order addresses the parties' discovery letter brief. It orders as follows:1. Topic 5. LinkedIn must designate and prepare one or more witnesses to testify, to the exte nt the information is known or reasonably available to it, to Topic 5 as written, subparts (a) through (d), including LinkedIns current and historical Azure workloads and systems; its purchases of Azure services and of GPU and other AI computing capa city from Microsoft, including prices and terms; its Azure spending, commitments, and forecasts; and its plans for future use of Azure.2. Topics 6 and 7. The designees must be prepared to testify to Topics 6 and 7 for the period from January 1, 20 14, to the present.3. Topic 7(c). LinkedIn must prepare its designee to testify about the topic subpart.4. Preparation. The designees must testify to information known or reasonably available to LinkedIn on the topics as scoped by this order; t hey may reasonably rely on and explain LinkedIn's produced documents and data and need not memorize granular data.5. Timing. The court understands that the depositions will take place on September 8, 2026.The attached order contains minimal redactions. The court will separately file an unredacted order under seal and will email an unredacted courtesy copy to the parties.Signed by Judge Laurel Beeler on 9/3/2026.(lblc2, COURT STAFF) (Filed on 9/3/2026)
